Team — I reviewed Vantage's redline and the items Jonas called out. Below are my notes and suggested redline text (paste into the Word doc).

1) Transfers / SCCs - We will sign the EU SCCs (2021 Standard Contractual Clauses) as an addendum. Suggested clause (short):
"Redwood will implement the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (EU Commission Implementing Decision 2021/914) as the transfer mechanism for EEA personal data. The SCCs will be executed as an addendum to this DPA, and the parties agree that the SCCs govern transfers from the Controller to the Processor to the extent required by applicable law."

Rationale: this preserves Vantage's requirement for an explicit mechanism while keeping Redwood's standard execution process. If Vantage prefers insertion of the full SCCs text in the DPA, we can accommodate but recommend an addendum for maintainability.

2) Subprocessors / notice window - We prefer a 30 day notice window. However, we can accept a 20-day notice for non-critical subprocessors. Suggested compromise language:
"Processor shall notify Controller of any new Subprocessor at least 30 days prior to authorizing the Subprocessor to process personal data. For Subprocessors categorized as non‑critical (operational SaaS providers), the notice period may be reduced to 20 days. Controller may object within the applicable notice period on reasonable grounds related to data protection; if parties cannot resolve the objection within 15 days, Processor may either (a) not appoint the Subprocessor or (b) provide reasonable mitigation measures acceptable to Controller."

3) Audit reports & attestations - We will deliver our SOC 2 Type II report. We cannot provide raw audit logs or customer-identifiable data, but will provide redacted reports and a SOC attestation within 30 days post-execution. Suggested addition: "Processor shall provide Controller with its most recent SOC 2 Type II report within 30 days of written request following execution; reports will be redacted to remove other customers' identifying information."

4) Liability & carveouts - Vantage's proposed unlimited liability for data transfer breaches is not acceptable. We should push for a negotiated cap tied to fees. Recommend keeping liability cap discussion with sales. Marissa — can you confirm Vantage's flexibility here?

5) Operational note: we should attach our subprocessors list and SCCs matrix to the DPA via a single-source link instead of embedding long tables. I'll prepare the subprocessors extract and the SCCs reference matrix (SCCs_reference_matrix.pdf) for the e-sign packet.

Please let me know if Vantage insists on a 15-day notice; we'll escalate but likely need additional contractual mitigations for critical subprocessors.

Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
